criteria.text: The participant has a histologically or cytologically confirmed metastatic or unresectable solid malignancy, specifically epithelial ovarian cancer, primary peritoneal cancer, or fallopian tube cancer; endometrial cancer; non-small cell lung cancer (Part A); EGFR-mutated NSCLC (Part B); breast cancer (hormone receptor positive, HER2-negative and triple-negative) (Part A); mesothelioma; or cervical cancer (Part B).

source.text: Histologically or cytologically confirmed metastatic or unresectable solid malignancy including ovarian cancer (must have epithelial ovarian cancer, primary peritoneal cancer, or fallopian tube cancer), endometrial cancer, non-small cell lung cancer (Part A), EGFR-mutated NSCLC (Part B), breast cancer (hormone receptor positive, HER2-negative and triple-negative) (Part A), mesothelioma or cervical cancer (Part B).

criteria.text: The participant has previously received therapies known to confer clinical benefit.

criteria.text: The participant has measurable disease per RECIST v1.1 at baseline (or mRECIST v1.1 for pleural mesothelioma).

source.text: Measurable disease per RECIST v1.1 for all tumor types other than pleural mesothelioma which will use mRECIST v1.1 at baseline.

criteria.text: The participant has a histologically or cytologically confirmed metastatic or unresectable epithelial ovarian cancer.

source.text: Participants must have histologically or cytologically confirmed metastatic or unresectable epithelial ovarian cancer as specified below.

criteria.text: The participant has high grade serous ovarian cancer, primary peritoneal cancer, or fallopian tube cancer (excluding endometrioid, clear cell carcinomas, mucinous, low grade, and those with a sarcomatous or neuroendocrine element).

source.text: High grade serous ovarian cancer, primary peritoneal cancer, or fallopian tube cancer (excluding endometrioid, clear cell carcinomas, mucinous, low grade, and those with a sarcomatous or neuroendocrine element)

criteria.text: The participant has received up to 3 prior lines of therapy (or up to 4 if MIRV was the last line and is locally approved), and has progressed radiographically on or after their most recent line of therapy.

source.text: Participants must have received up to 3 prior lines of therapy. Participants may have had up to to 4 prior lines of therapy are allowed if MIRV is locally approved and was used as the last line of therapy. Participants must have progressed radiographically on or after their most recent line of therapy.

source.text: Participants must have received prior bevacizumab or approved biosimilar.

criteria.text: If the participant has a known or suspected deleterious germline or somatic BRCA mutation and achieved a complete or partial response to platinum-based chemotherapy, they must have been treated with a PARP inhibitor as maintenance treatment.

source.text: Participants with known or suspected deleterious germline or somatic BRCA mutations (as determined by Food and Drug Administration \[FDA\]-approved test in a Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments \[CLIA\]-certified laboratory; or locally approved equivalent) and who achieved a complete or partial response to platinum-based chemotherapy must have been treated with a poly ADP-ribose polymerase (PARP) inhibitor as maintenance treatment.

criteria.text: If the participant has primary platinum-refractory ovarian cancer, they must have received ≤2 prior lines of therapy. (Primary platinum-refractory ovarian cancer is defined as a lack of response or progression within 91 days after completing front-line platinum containing therapy).

source.text: Participants with primary platinum-refractory ovarian cancer must have received ≤2 prior lines of therapy. Primary platinum-refractory ovarian cancer is defined as a lack of response or by progression within 91 days after completing front-line platinum containing therapy.

criteria.text: The participant has received 1 to 3 prior lines of therapy for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC), and up to 4 prior lines of therapy for platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC).

source.text: Participants must have received 1 to 3 prior lines of therapy for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC), and up to 4 prior lines of therapy for platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC). Prior treatments may have included bevacizumab, PARP inhibitor, and MIRV.

criteria.text: If the participant has platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC), they must have disease progression on or after maintenance treatment, or at least 6 months (>183 days) or more from the last dose of platinum-based therapy.

source.text: Participants with PSOC must have disease progression on or after maintenance treatment, or at least 6 months (\>183 days) or more from the last dose of platinum-based therapy.

The participant has previously received all therapies known to confer clinical benefit (unless ineligible to receive, refused to receive, or therapy is unavailable in the region). If a standard-of-care therapy is available that has not been administered, the reason that the therapy is not appropriate must be documented.

source.text: Participants must have a histologically or cytologically confirmed metastatic or unresectable solid malignancy. criteria.text: The participant has either ovarian cancer (must have high grade epithelial ovarian cancer, primary peritoneal cancer, or fallopian tube cancer including serous, endometrioid, and clear cell carcinomas, and excluding mucinous, low grade, and those with a sarcomatous or neuroendocrine element), or NSCLC.

source.text:
Participants must either have ovarian cancer (must have high grade epithelial ovarian cancer, primary peritoneal cancer, or fallopian tube cancer including serous, endometrioid, and clear cell carcinomas, and excluding mucinous, low grade, and those with a sarcomatous or neuroendocrine element), or
* NSCLC.
